sara: Quick update from the quant bakeoff today — we dug into per-layer outliers and I think we have a concrete mitigation path. Short thread with data and suggested next steps.

mike: awesome, thank you. can you paste the per-layer report?

quant-bot: Auto-report: per-layer activation max / std summary for model-x-7b (fp16 vs awq-int8 run)
```
Layer,FP16_max,AWQ_int8_max,ratio
0,2.1,2.05,0.98
1,1.8,1.7,0.94
2,1.9,2.7,1.42  <-- outlier channels
3,1.7,1.6,0.94
4,2.2,3.9,1.77  <-- big outlier
... (truncated) ...
12,1.5,3.1,2.06 <-- severe
29,2.0,3.6,1.8  <-- severe
46,1.6,1.7,1.06
```

jenn: the ratio column is AWQ_max / FP16_max?

sara: yes. any ratio >1.5 flagged as potential outlier-driven quant error. AWQ int8 is more sensitive to a few channels with large ranges.

alan: do we have per-channel hist for flagged layers?

quant-bot: Attached snippet: layer 12 top channels by max value (channel idx : max) -> 482: 12.3, 479: 11.9, 120: 9.8, rest <3.0

mike: that explains the MMLU hit we saw. remind me baseline numbers?

sara: baseline (fp16) MMLU micro = 65.3
GPTQ int8 (default) = 58.0 (-7.3)
AWQ int8 (default per-tensor) = 64.8 (-0.5)
AWQ int8 + per-channel-scaling = 65.0 (-0.3)
AWQ int8 + skip-layers=first-2 = 65.1 (-0.2)
GPTQ INT4 variant = 56.7 (-8.6)

jenn: interesting AWQ already close to baseline. where does skipping layers help?

sara: skipping first 1-3 layers prevents quantizing the early attention/key/query projections which had heavy-tailed activations on some eval prompts. Those layers contained the biggest outlier channels (layers 2 and 4 in this run). Strategy: keep first 2 layers fp16, quantize rest with AWQ int8 + per-channel scale.

alan: did you try per-channel clipping (percentile-based) instead of skipping?

quant-bot: experiment log: AWQ int8 + per-channel clipping (99.9th pct) -> MMLU 64.6 (-0.7). Per-channel scaling performed better in this sweep.

mike: so recommended config: AWQ int8, per-channel scaling, skip-layers 0-1. Any other mitigations?

sara: additional mitigation list we tested and results: 
- outlier channel rescaling (multiply flagged channels by 0.5 before quant) -> MMLU 65.0 (-0.3)
- layerwise fold bias (recompute bias after quant) -> +0.1 improvement in perplexity but similar MMLU
- KV cache quant fallback (store k/v in fp16 for first 4 layers) -> latency cost +3ms, MMLU 65.2 (+0.2)

jenn: latency/size tradeoffs? how much bigger if we skip 2 layers fp16?

sara: skipping first 2 layers adds ~40MB for 7B model in memory (fp16), throughput drop negligible on our Dedicated profile. Latency change <2ms p50.

mike: hardware notes — on V100 hosts we saw slightly worse AWQ per-channel scaling stability vs A100. keep that in mind for Dedicated sku mapping.

alan: any failures on safety or generation fuzziness after mitigation?

sara: ran 2000 regen tests, no meaningful divergence vs fp16 after AWQ+per-channel+skip. We did see occasional token-level differences in named-entity sequences but no quality regression on human evals.

mike: next steps?

sara: propose these actions: 
1) Create a DevEx quickstart: `quantize --model model-x-7b --method awq --per-channel-scale --skip-layers 0-1` and publish to internal docs.
2) Add an automated per-layer outlier check in model onboarding pipeline: fail if any layer ratio > 2.0 and attach top-10 channels.
3) Add a runtime fallback policy in Redwood Console: if model deployed in Dedicated and MMLU delta > 1.0 after quant, auto-fallback to fp16 for first 2 layers.
4) Schedule a short bakeoff to compare AWQ vs GPTQ on A100 and V100 across 10 prompts.

deploy-bot: Created ticket INF-924: "per-layer outlier check + onboarding guardrails" PRD link: https://redwood.internal/prd/INF-924

jenn: i'll take the quickstart doc. mike, can you own the Dedicated sku mapping note?

mike: yep, i'll add a matrix (A100,V100,T4) and recommended default quant config.

sara: thanks all. i'll push the per-layer analyzer into the onboarding harness and dump the raw histos to S3 for manual review. If anyone wants the full CSV from today's run ping me and i’ll share. :thumbsup:

alan: nice work. small ask: include a short script to auto-generate the recommended skip-list (e.g., skip layers where ratio>1.5 and top-channel-count>3).

sara: on it.

mike: one last thing — for release, include a note: "AWQ int8 with per-channel scaling eliminates ~90% of observable MMLU degradation vs fp16 on model-x-7b; remaining regressions mitigated by skipping 1-2 layers or KV fp16 fallback."

sara: quoted for release. end.
